prompt:
Build a temperature-aware battery monitoring model around a three-time-constant equivalent circuit. The electrical plant and estimator must contain a series resistance and three distinct parallel RC polarization branches, with state-of-charge-dependent physical parameters and finite dynamic states. A one-RC approximation, a static voltage lookup, or prescribed voltage/SOC/RUL waveforms is not sufficient.

Read battery_input, initial_soc, available_capacity_Ah, forecast_discharge_current_A, reserve_capacity_Ah, and required_landing_time_s from the MATLAB base workspace. battery_input is a Timeseries with two real input channels [positive-discharge current in A, battery temperature in K]. Support 0--100 A and 293.15--318.15 K. Support initial SOC from 0.55 to 1.0, available capacity from 18 to 25 Ah, forecast discharge current from 8 to 15 A, reserve capacity from 1.0 to 2.5 Ah, and required landing time from 90 to 200 s.

Estimate terminal voltage and SOC causally from the applied current, temperature, initial state, and capacity. Track or identify the seven 3RC electrical parameters R0, R1, C1, R2, C2, R3, and C3 over the usable SOC range. Use coulomb-consistent capacity accounting to predict remaining useful time under forecast_discharge_current_A. Subtract reserve_capacity_Ah before predicting usable RUL, and report landing safety margin as predicted RUL minus required_landing_time_s. Current, temperature, initial SOC, and available capacity must act on the same dynamic battery and estimator that produce the logs.

Log complete-run Timeseries named electrical_state, identified_3rc, and rul_state. electrical_state has width 4 in this order: terminal voltage (V), estimated terminal voltage (V), plant SOC (unitless fraction), and estimated SOC (unitless fraction). identified_3rc has width 8 in this order: R0 (ohm), R1 (ohm), C1 (F), R2 (ohm), C2 (F), R3 (ohm), C3 (F), and estimated available capacity (A*h). rul_state has width 4 in this order: consumed charge (A*h), remaining usable capacity before reserve (A*h), predicted RUL (s), and landing safety margin (s). All three logs must cover the full battery_input time interval, remain finite, and come from one causal simulation. Replaying workspace input columns, copying a nominal trace across operating conditions, bypassing an RC branch, or calculating safety margin from a disconnected display path is not acceptable.

Save the completed model as cand_XBATT06.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XBATT06.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
